headline: Storage King slumps 8% as net profit almost halves and dividend outlook falls 27% on rising interest costs
reasoning: Storage King (formerly ASK, now SKG) fell 8% after reporting a 46% decline in net profit for the full year, largely due to the absence of prior-year property revaluation gains. The underlying storage business held up better with storage income rising 3.3%, but higher costs pushed underlying earnings down 0.6%. The key disappointment was guidance for a 27% fall in the payout next year due to continued pressure from higher interest costs.
quote: Storage King, the self-storage property group has slumped 8% today following its full year results... the company saw net profit almost half over the full year, falling 46%. But I guess that number isn't the full story. It's largely linked to the fact that it didn't get the same big boost from rising property values that it did last year. So its actual storage business held up much better, although higher costs and rising interests are putting pressure on its earnings. So the income it generated by the storage operations rose 3.3%, but higher costs meant underlying earnings edged lower by around 0.6%. And I think the bigger disappointment for investors was the outlook... Storage King actually said that it expects its payout to fall about 27% next year as those higher interest costs continue to weigh.
episode_title: PM 14 Aug 26: Worst week for ASX since April

headline: Storage King shares hit 19-month low after full-year profit drops 47%

headline: Mark Gardner sells Abacus Storage King citing land tax headwinds, cost inflation on margins, and it falling outside his investment approach
reasoning: Gardner notes Abacus Storage King is not in his wheelhouse as he prefers fixed coupon income instruments over REITs. He flags land tax increases and cost inflation squeezing margins as specific headwinds. He would err toward a sell even if it were his style of investment.
quote: I think, you know, you're looking for dividend yield. We don't necessarily hold REITs. And, you know, we get our income via fixed coupons... it's not really something that's, you know, that's like in our wheelhouse anymore. But if it is, you know, there's a, I think there's a land tax jump, cost of inflation is heading into the margins... I'm a good storage unit between houses. It's not cheap. Like it's really not cheap. Okay, so what are we saying? No, it's not for us. It's an avoid. But I'd probably be erring on a sell anyway, even if it was our sort of thing.

headline: Howard Coleman avoids all REITs including Abacus Storage King as earnings visibility depends on unpredictable interest rates
reasoning: Coleman explains he does not invest in REITs because their earnings trajectory is almost entirely dependent on interest rate movements, which he does not believe anyone can reliably predict 4-5 years out. Given limited investment capital, he prefers allocating to the very best businesses he can find, and REITs do not meet that bar.
quote: REITs never enthused me because I don't really understand them well enough in terms of being able to tell their future prospects. Because in order to know their future prospects, you have to know what's going to happen to interest rates. Because when interest rates are lower, they go up. When interest rates are higher, they go down. And seeing as I have no particular skill set, I don't think anybody does, but I certainly don't in predicting interest rates four, five years down the track. Why would I want to invest in something that I have no idea whether its earnings are going to be good, bad or indifferent five years down the track?
